title: Giving
note: This means giving, without refusing, to the poor who ask. It looks to the next life, so it follows the duty to the world, which looks to this one.

couplets.plain: Only giving to those who have nothing is giving. All else is like a loan, measured out and paid back.
couplets.pm: Only giving what they need to those who have nothing is truly giving. All other gifts, made to those who aren’t poor for some gain, are like a loan measured out and paid back in the same measure, because they come back to you.

links.quote: Only giving to those who have nothing is giving

couplets.plain: Even if it were a good road, taking is bad. Even if there were no higher world, giving is good.
couplets.pm: Even if some said that taking is the good road to the world of liberation, it is bad. Even if some said that givers don’t reach that world, giving is good. “Even if” shows that no one says such things. Giving ranks above the other righteous acts.
couplets.sensitive: calls receiving help a bad thing

links.quote: Even if there were no higher world, giving is good

couplets.plain: Never speaking the misery of “I have nothing”, and giving: these belong only to those of good birth.
couplets.pm: Two things are found only in the well-born: not telling others the shame of “I am poor”, as a beggar does, and not refusing those who say it to you. Others read it as giving before someone has to ask, giving so that they need ask no one else, or giving with no plea of “I have nothing now”.
couplets.note: “Never speaking” can belong to the giver or the asker. He takes it as never begging yourself, which makes two things, as the plural verb suggests.

links.quote: Never speaking the misery of “I have nothing”, and giving
Never speaking the misery of “I have nothing”, and giving
links.reason: Tells the person being asked to give, with no talk of having nothing.

couplets.plain: Being begged from is painful, until you see the pleased face of the one who begged.
couplets.pm: Not only begging but being begged from is painful, until you see the face of the one who begged made sweet by getting it. Being begged from means resolving to give to all who beg. It pains you for fear you may fail someone. So you must give everything you have.

links.quote: until you see the pleased face of the one who begged
until you see the pleased face of the one who begged

couplets.plain: The strength of the strong is to bear hunger. It comes after the strength of those who end that hunger.
couplets.pm: The strength of those made strong by austerity is to bear the hunger that comes to them. But it comes after the strength of those who end such hunger by giving. Better than going hungry and being unable to end another’s hunger is to be free of hunger yourself and end theirs.

links.quote: It comes after the strength of those who end that hunger
links.reason: Ending hunger outranks even the strength of bearing your own.

couplets.plain: End the ruinous hunger of those who have nothing. That is where someone who has wealth can store it.
couplets.pm: End the great hunger of the poor, for the sake of righteousness. That righteousness is where someone who has wealth stores it for their own later use. Hunger is called ruinous because it destroys all that is good. The wealth spent on ending it comes back to help you.

links.quote: End the ruinous hunger of those who have nothing
links.reason: Ending the hunger of those with nothing is given as the proper use of wealth.

links.quote: where someone who has wealth can store it
links.reason: Ending hunger is pictured as the place to store your wealth.

couplets.plain: The evil disease called hunger will hardly touch someone used to sharing their food.
couplets.pm: The evil disease called hunger doesn’t touch someone who always shares their food. It is evil because it destroys knowledge and conduct in this body and brings suffering to the bodies that follow. Such a person is their own physician, so the disease can’t come near.

links.quote: someone used to sharing their food
links.reason: Sharing your food is what keeps hunger from ever reaching you.

couplets.plain: Do they not know the joy of giving and being glad, those hard-hearted people who hoard what they own and lose it?
couplets.pm: Those without compassion keep what they own without giving and later lose it. Have they never seen the joy the compassionate have from giving to the poor and seeing them glad? If they knew it, they would have that joy themselves, and would not hoard and lose.

links.quote: hoard what they own and lose it
Do they not know the joy of giving

couplets.plain: Surely more painful than begging is eating alone what you have piled up.
couplets.pm: To give nothing to the poor and eat alone, in order to fill a shortfall of wealth, is surely worse than begging. That means setting a figure and piling up stingily to reach it. Begging holds only the moment’s shame, with no poverty after. Eating alone has both. Some read it as the food you have gathered.
couplets.note: நிரப்பிய can mean what you have piled up, as the plain reading takes it, or, as he reads it, in order to fill up a shortfall of wealth.

links.quote: eating alone what you have piled up
links.reason: Eating your hoard alone is made worse than begging.

couplets.plain: Nothing is more painful than dying. Even that is sweet when you can’t give.
couplets.pm: Nothing is as painful as dying. Even dying is sweet when you can’t give anything to the poor, because it rids you of the weight of a body that is no use to others.
couplets.sensitive: calls death sweet when one cannot give

links.quote: Even that is sweet when you can’t give
